title: Branch access and head-office approval conflict
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Maintenance provider for multi-site retail and education groups; one customer has 28 branches.
owner_narrative: Head office pays and approves parts, but branches call and control access. Branches expect appointments before approval arrives. Equipment moves between similar-named locations. Several apparently separate failures turned out to follow one central configuration change.

diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Head office approves cost; the branch agrees access.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Similar symptoms across branches may be independent hardware faults; common timing is a hypothesis, not proof.

evidence.description: A simulated move record conflicts with the asset sheet.
Simulated tickets share a configuration-change timestamp.
A simulated approval matrix separates branch and central authority.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Customer hierarchy, device location and approval dependencies are not modelled consistently.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: Similar symptoms across branches may be independent hardware faults; common timing is a hypothesis, not proof.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Establish organization/site/device identities and separate access approval from spending approval; retain local child tickets under confirmed shared incidents.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Link related incidents for review; route approvals to scoped authorities; provide role-filtered views and readiness checks.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Do not expose another branch’s restricted data.
requirements.rationale: Customer hierarchy, device location and approval dependencies are not modelled consistently.

requirements.statement: A planned appointment is not confirmed until required approvals and access exist.
requirements.rationale: Customer hierarchy, device location and approval dependencies are not modelled consistently.

requirements.statement: Parent incident closure does not prove every branch is restored.
requirements.rationale: Customer hierarchy, device location and approval dependencies are not modelled consistently.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Similar branch names resolve by stable IDs.
Moving an asset preserves historical visits at the old site.
Restoring two branches leaves the third child ticket open.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Hierarchical incidents, effective asset locations and scoped approval routing are extensions.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Repeat trips caused by missing approval or incorrect location / branch service visits.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Establish organization/site/device identities and separate access approval from spending approval; retain local child tickets under confirmed shared incidents. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: Similar symptoms across branches may be independent hardware faults; common timing is a hypothesis, not proof.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Organization hierarchy, approver limits and actual shared dependencies need confirmation.
